scope: Theorem 8.1 (Magnetic-field extension) of the manuscript “All-temperature pressure for orthogonally invariant Ising spin glasses” (preprints/All-temperature-pressure-for-orthogonally-invariant-Ising-spin-glasses-September-25-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 234 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 ecaeb31108feca6f), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF pages 48-49. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. The quote crosses a page break and includes whatever the extraction places there, such as a page number. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. statement: Assume the deterministic spectral hypotheses of The- orem 1.1, with limiting compactly supported law μ. Suppose first that the field values belong to a fixed finite alphabet c1, . . . , cJ ∈ R, and that the proportion of sites with value cj tends to a positive rational number γj. Then PN (c(N)) converges in expectation and almost surely to Fμ ⎛ ⎝ J ∑︂ j=1 γjδcj ⎞ ⎠ = sup m∈((−1,1)∩Q)J ⎧ ⎨ ⎩ J ∑︂ j=1 γjcjmj + inf p∈P [︁ Sm(p) + G1(p) ]︁ ⎫ ⎬ ⎭ . (8.4) 48 More generally, suppose the empirical field laws converge in the first-moment transport metric W1 to a probability law ν on R with finite absolute first moment. Then the same modes of convergence hold, with limit Fμ(ν), where Fμ(ν) = lim q→∞ Fμ(νq) (8.5) for any finite-support laws νq with positive rational masses such that W1(νq, ν) → 0. This limit exists and is independent of the approximating sequence.
